statement.p: Convert the following point from rectangular to spherical coordinates: \left(\frac{ 5\sqrt{6}}{4},\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{4},\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right).
Usage: To enter a point, for example (x,y,z), type "(x, y, z)".

static.solution:
x=\frac{ 5\sqrt{6}}{4}, y=\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{4}, and z=\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{2}. The radial coordinate is \rho=\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}=\sqrt{\textstyle \left(\frac{ 5\sqrt{6}}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2}=5. The angular coordinate \theta satisfies \tan \theta=\frac{y}{x}=\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}/4}{ 5\sqrt{6}/4}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} so either \theta=\frac{ \pi}{6} or \theta=\frac{7 \pi}{6}. Since the point (x,y)=(\frac{ 5\sqrt{6}}{4},\frac{ 5\sqrt{2}}{4}) is in the first quadrant, the correct choice is \theta=\frac{ \pi}{6}. The angle of declination \phi satisfies \cos \phi=\frac{z}{\rho}=\frac{ \sqrt{2}}{2}, \qquad 0\leq \phi\leq \pi and so \phi=\frac{ \pi}{4}.
The spherical coordinates are thus (\rho,\theta,\phi)=\left(5,\frac{ \pi}{6},\frac{ \pi}{4}\right).
